newsitem.title: USA: U.S. sues Raymark for $192 mln toxic waste cleanup.
newsitem.headline: U.S. sues Raymark for $192 mln toxic waste cleanup.

text.p: The U.S. government Tuesday sued Raymark Industries Inc for past and future cleanup costs, estimated at more than $192 million, at a toxic waste site in Stratford, Connecticut.

The company allegedly dumped lead, asbestos, PCBs (polychorinated biphenyls) and other hazardous materials from its brake linings and friction products business for seventy years up to 1989 at the Raymark Industries Superfund Site and other locations in Stratford, according to the Justice Department.
The state of Connecticut also sued to recover $20 million which it expects to spend for its share of cleanup costs.

The federal lawsuit also targets Roderick Laukhuff, alleging that Raymark fraudulently transferred ownership of the toxic waste site to Laukhuff as soon as EPA told the company it was going to put a lien on the property.
Laukhuff was not immediately available for comment.
